entries.description: Order Of St. Michael and St. George
Silver, Large P, D, or S above Monticello

notes.text: Book pages 202-203. Medals section (section heading not visible on this page; appears to continue the Canadian medals listings from the previous page). Under Victoria Cross, the sub-row 'Awarded to a Canadian' (65,000.00) is printed directly beneath the Victoria Cross row (40,000.00).

Book page 204. COINS OF THE UNITED STATES. MINT MARKS: C - Charlotte, North Carolina; CC - Carson City, Nevada; D - Dahlonega, Georgia (gold coins only); D - Denver, Colorado (1906 to date); O - New Orleans, Louisiana; S - San Francisco, California; P - Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.
Book page 204. IMPORTANT: Buying prices are for coins in VG condition. Coins in lesser grades such as Good or About Good will command lower buying prices.
Book page 205. Footnote under SMALL CENTS / Flying Eagle: '* Counterfeits exist' (applies to 1856*).

Book page 205. The Classic Head large cent table (1808 to 1812 to 1814) is partially cut at the spine; prices were aligned to dates accounting for page skew: 1808 30.00, 1809 60.00, 1810 25.00, 1811 40.00, 1812 to 1814 25.00.
Book page 210. Washington - Silver table: key-date rows 1932D and 1932S prices were at the edge of legibility (read as 20.00 and 50.00); flagged uncertain.
Book page 213. 2006S Nevada, PR price ambiguous in scan (read as either 1.25 or 2.00; every other State Quarters PR row is 1.25); price set to null and flagged uncertain.

Book page 215. Note: MS is Mint State, uncirculated business strike. PR is Proof Condition, collector coins of high quality mirror finish. Silver Proofs are .900 fine silver coins with a high quality mirror finish.
Book page 217. Note: Silver dollars must grade very good (VG) or better to command prices listed.
